1. Aggrieved by the judgment and award dated 19.02.2019 passed in MVC No.6716/2017 by the XVIII Additional Judge, Court of Small Causes, Member, MACT, Bengaluru (for short 'the Tribunal'), the petitioner therein has preferred this appeal.

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. For the sake of convenience, the parties are referred to herein as per their status before the Tribunal.

3. Brief facts of the case are as follows:
On 17.04.2017, at about 11.30 a.m., while the petitioner was crossing Mysore road from East to west direction near Nayandahalli bus stop, Bengaluru, at that time, a two wheeler Mahindra Gusto-125, bearing Engine No.UIE-GF004089, being driven in a rash and negligent manner dashed against the petitioner.

Due to which, the petitioner sustained the following injuries:
i. Abrasion over lateral aspect of right leg.
ii. Lacerated wound over right occipital region 2x1 cms.

iii. Tenderness over lateral aspect of right leg(upper).

sentences.text:
The Tribunal, based on the evidence let in, came to the conclusion that the accident happened due to rash and negligent driving of the motor cycle which was duly insured with respondent No.2 and respondent No.2 is liable to pay a compensation of Rs.1,46000/- along with interest @ 6% p.a.
under the following heads:-
SL. HEADS OF COMPENSATION AMOUNT NO. IN RS.
1. Pain and sufferings 30,000 2.

Medical expenses 13,000 3. Loss of income during the period of 24,000 treatment 4. Disability 39,000 5. Towards food, conveyance, 20,000 nourishment and attendant charges 6. Loss of future amenities and 20,000 happiness Total
Not satisfied by the same, the petitioner has preferred this appeal.
5. Admittedly, the accident happened in the year 2017.
The petitioner at the time of accident was aged about 77 years.
She is said to be a goldsmith.
But she has not produced any proof before the Tribunal.
The treated doctor has stated that she has a permanent disability of 30% to her right lower limb.
The Tribunal has taken the permanent disability to the whole body at 8%.
In my opinion, the same is on the lower side and 10% would be appropriate, which is 1/3rd of the disability to the right lower limb.
The accident being of the year 2017, as per the Lok Adalath chart, Rs.11,000/- is considered as her notional income.
Given her age, the Tribunal has taken multiplier at '5' and the same is retained.
Thus, towards 'loss of future income' the petitioner is entitled to a sum of Rs.66,000/- (Rs.11,000x12x5x10%) as against Rs.39,000/- awarded by the Tribunal.

Towards loss of income during the laid up period, the petitioner is entitled to a sum of Rs.33,000/- (Rs.11,000x3)
as against Rs.24,000/- awarded by the Tribunal.
Towards the head 'Pain and suffering', a sum of Rs.30,000/- is awarded by the Tribunal.
I deem the same to be appropriate.
Towards 'Medical expenses, a sum of Rs.13,000/- is awarded based on the actual bills.
I deem the same to be appropriate.

Towards food, conveyance, nourishment and attendant charges a sum of Rs.20,000/-
is awarded by the Tribunal.
I deem the same to be appropriate.
Towards 'loss of future amenities and happiness', the Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.20,000/-.
Given the nature of injuries, I deem it appropriate to enhance it to Rs.30,000/-.
6. Thus, the compensation awarded to the petitioner under different heads is modified as hereunder:-

COMPENSATION COMPENSATION AWARDED SL. HEADS OF AWARDED BY BEFORE NO. COMPENSATION THIS COURT TRIBUNAL (AMT. IN RS.) (AMT. IN RS.)

sentences.text: 1. Pain and 30,000 30,000 sufferings 2.
Medical expenses 13,000 13,000 3. Loss of income 24,000 33,000 during the period of treatment
4. Loss of future 39,000 66,000 income 5. Towards food, 20,000 20,000 conveyance, nourishment and attendant charges 6. Loss of future 20,000 30,000 amenities and happiness Total 1,46,000 1,92,000

Thus, the petitioner would be entitled to a total compensation of Rs.1,92,000/- as against Rs.1,46,000/-
awarded by the Tribunal.

7. Hence, the following:
ORDER i) Appeal is allowed in part;
ii) The total compensation awarded by the Tribunal is modified and enhanced to Rs.1,92,000/- as against Rs.1,46,000/-
awarded by the Tribunal along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of filing of the petition before the Tribunal till the date of realization.

iii) Respondent No.2 shall pay to the petitioner the enhanced compensation of Rs.46,000/- along with interest @ 6% per annum from the date of petition before the Tribunal till realization in addition to what has been awarded by the Tribunal within a period of six weeks from the date of receipt of certified copy of this order.
iv) Registry is directed to send the records to the jurisdictional Tribunal.
v) Draw modified award accordingly.
